prompt: A ski resort's profit fell 20% in a season when visits were flat. The candidate's framework: (1) Visits: day tickets and season passes; (2) Ticket and pass prices; (3) Costs: staff, snowmaking and lift maintenance. What is the flaw in this framework?

options.text: Buckets 1 and 2 overlap: pass prices decide how many passes sell
options.feedback: Price affects volume, but visits and prices are separate drivers of ticket revenue.

options.text: Bucket 1 doesn't belong: visits were flat, so they can't explain the drop
options.feedback: Flat visits are a finding, not a reason to drop the bucket. The split between day tickets and passes can still move revenue.

options.text: It's a generic profit tree: ski resorts depend on the weather
options.feedback: Weather works through visits and snowmaking costs, which are in the tree. The flaw is a missing revenue stream.

options.text: Missing: what visitors spend on rentals, lessons and food
options.feedback: Right. Tickets are only part of a resort's revenue. With visits flat, lower spending on rentals, lessons and food could explain the drop.

explanation: Revenue = visits × (ticket price + spending on the mountain). The framework covers tickets but not rentals, lessons and food.

extras.corrected_framework: Visits (day tickets, passes); ticket and pass prices; spending per visit (rentals, lessons, food); costs
